The assigned source states x(n)=nL for integers n>=0 and identifies L as a length scale. It assigns no time map t(n) and no clock interval. Thus n labels positions; its index increment is not an elapsed time. The source determines the spatial step x(n+1)-x(n)=L, but speed requires a distance divided by an elapsed time. No propagation speed, numerical value of c, or identification with c follows from the assigned facts alone.

A proposed additional clock rule is t(n)=n tau, where tau is a fixed finite positive time interval with units of time. This rule is an assumption introduced here, not a rule contained in the source. Conditional on that rule, for any integers m>n>=0, the interval velocity is [x(m)-x(n)]/[t(m)-t(n)]=(m-n)L/[(m-n)tau]=L/tau. Its dimensions are length/time. The corresponding speed is |L|/tau; under the positive-length convention L>0, it is L/tau. Every finite positive tau gives a compatible time assignment and a potentially different speed. Replacing tau by a tau for any dimensionless a>0 leaves x(n) unchanged and divides the conditional speed by a, demonstrating that the assigned positions cannot select it.

This conditional result describes average motion between assigned samples. A claim about instantaneous speed between samples needs a further interpolation or dynamical assumption; for example, proposing x(t)=(L/tau)t for t>=0 would give constant continuous velocity. Neither interpolation nor dynamics is assigned. The finite positive clock interval excludes a zero denominator; the formal limit tau approaching zero from above grows without bound for a fixed positive L and supplies no physical prediction or bound. The assigned index domain gives no information about negative-time behavior.

To call this conditional speed c, one must additionally define what c denotes and supply either an explicit model relation identifying it with this motion or independent evidence tying the spatial steps to elapsed time for the stated propagation process. If c is intended as a universal or invariant physical propagation constant, that interpretation and its applicability also require evidence or governing assumptions beyond this packet. Choosing tau=L/c merely imposes a desired value (for positive L and c); it does not derive c. This is source-grounded algebra and dimensional reasoning only, with no validated physics or Aether-Flow result claim.
